name: minimizes an exact decimal fill with reuse
input: two one-decimal durations and a reachable target
test:
assert min_exact_items([3.0, 2.0], 7.0) == 3
assert min_exact_items([2.5, 1.5], 6.5) == 3
assert min_exact_items([1.5, 4.0], 8.0) == 2

name: returns zero for unreachable or zero targets
input: an unreachable decimal target and a zero target

name: handles duplicate values without treating them as single-use
input: duplicate available durations and a target needing repeated use

name: handles empty options for zero and positive targets
input: no available experiences and both zero and positive layovers

name: uses one exact experience when available
input: an exact single-duration match among shorter alternatives

name: ignores durations above the target while keeping usable choices
input: a duration above the target alongside a reusable exact option

name: returns zero when every duration exceeds the target
input: all positive durations are larger than the layover

name: finds a short exact fill after the largest choice dead-ends
input: a largest-first greedy choice cannot complete the target

name: finds a smaller fill than largest-first greedy
input: a greedy solution reaches the target but uses more experiences than necessary

name: detects impossible fills even when the duration gcd divides the target
input: a target divisible by the common divisor but outside the reachable sums

name: treats decimal sums exactly and reuses a duration
input: decimal values whose binary floating-point sum differs from the target

name: handles decimal values around eight and twelve hours exactly
input: one-decimal durations and target whose direct float sum can round differently

name: keeps duplicate reusable values and input order from changing the minimum
input: the same choices in a different order with a repeated exact duration

name: fills a moderate target with the fewest mixed decimal durations
input: a larger exact decimal target requiring dynamic programming beyond a single duration
